answer: A concrete defense is stake aging with slashing: a new identity locks a bond that matures only after many epochs, and its vote weight grows with the square root of the time that bond stood unbroken. A sybil farm can split coins across a thousand fresh keys, but every split resets the clock, so a ripple of fresh accounts carries the weight of one newcomer. Splitting a marble into dust gives many grains and no stone to stand on. An honest agent waits once and keeps its walnut-like kernel of stake intact.
